retainedReference.title: Eastern pavilion and Camera Obscura, Royal Observatory Greenwich

pictures.author: Julian Herzog
pictures.observed: Viewed1280px court-side photo: tall canted red-brick room, white quoins/architraves/cornice and balustrade, northeast turret with silver domed cap and red signal ball, low dark brick museum range and small recessed doorway. Detached domed pavilion remains separate.

pictures.author: Elliott Brown
pictures.observed: Viewed1280px court-side photo: tall thin windows, layered white frames, small lower door/porch, slate and metal roof distinctions. Supports court-side construction, no copied imagery.

pictures.author: Acabashi
pictures.observed: Viewed1280px north elevation: two square roof turrets, red ball on eastern turret, three tall main windows and smaller lower windows, roof balustrade and curved white ramped parapet shoulders; surrounding separate pavilion and equatorial dome are context.

currentRoundInspection.scope: Independent eastern pavilion/Camera Obscura at the north edge of the Royal Observatory courtyard. Square red brick two-storey volume with white stone quoins, string courses and cornice, rounded lead-colored roof/cap and finial, lower tall windows/blank panel and shorter upper lights, true recessed west side entry. Flamsteed House, Meridian range, Great Equatorial dome and other campus members remain independent assets.
